text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the appointed candidate are men, so an all-male panel could not have favored him over you on the basis of sex. Raising the panel's gender composition would undermine your credibility and distract from legitimate concerns.

Instead, focus on merit and procedural transparency. You possess formal leadership qualifications—a master's degree and five years of deputy principal experience—while the appointee primarily has classroom teaching experience and coursework. Rather than questioning the panel's demographics, send a polite follow-up requesting the written feedback you were promised, asking specifically how administrative qualifications and interview performance were weighted in the final decision.
